title: Standard builds for existing Pro teams have moved to usage-based billing
description: Existing Pro teams will no longer include a Standard build slot. This brings Standard builds under the same usage-based billing model as other build machines. Standard builds cost $0.014 per build minute, and your monthly usage credit applies to build usage. Billing applies to all projects on the team. title: All Sandbox runtimes now use Vercel Managed Images
description: All Vercel Sandbox runtimes now use Vercel Managed Images (VMIs). Legacy runtimes, such as node22 , now use the open-source images in the vercel/sandbox repository , distributed through Vercel Container Registry (VCR). Sandboxes created with these now come with 64 GB of storage and use the same infrastructure as sandboxes powered by VCR. The universal image is released nightly, and rolling tags such as latest pick up operating system, dependency, and coding agent updates. Pin an image digest when you need a reproducible environment. Sandboxes created with version 3 or later of the JavaScript Sandbox SDK use vercel/sandbox/universal:latest by default. The universal image includes Node.js, Python, coding agents such as Claude Code and Pi, and common utilities. You can pull it at vcr.vercel.com/vercel/sandbox/universal:latest . Learn more in the Sandbox documentation . Read more

title: AWS PrivateLink endpoints are now available on Secure Compute
description: Enterprise teams using Secure Compute can now create and manage AWS PrivateLink endpoints directly from the Vercel dashboard. Endpoints on Secure Compute live in your team's dedicated VPC and use the network's AWS region. They belong to the network and are shared by its connected project environments. Vercel Functions , Vercel Sandbox , and builds connected to the network can reach AWS-hosted backends over the AWS private network. Before you add an endpoint in Vercel, the backend must already be exposed through a published AWS PrivateLink endpoint service. Examples include RDS, Aurora, Redshift, Snowflake, MongoDB Atlas, and internal services behind a Network Load Balancer. In Team Settings → Networking , open your Secure Compute network and choose Add Endpoint from the PrivateLink tab. Standard pricing for new endpoints: Each Secure Compute network includes one AWS PrivateLink endpoint. Additional endpoints cost $30 per month each. PrivateLink data transfer costs $0.04 per GB. Read the Secure Compute PrivateLink documentation to get started. Read more

title: Flags SDK now works on Vercel without FLAGS_SECRET
description: With flags@4.5.0 , projects on Vercel can use Flags Explorer and precompute without FLAGS_SECRET . That cuts out a setup step for new projects and removes the need to keep a shared secret in sync across microfrontends. Vercel signs Flags Explorer discovery requests and overrides, and the SDK encrypts flag values shown in the Vercel Toolbar with Vercel’s public key. Existing projects keep using FLAGS_SECRET while the environment variable is set or the secret is passed in code. Upgrading alone doesn't switch them to Vercel-managed keys. To use Vercel-managed keys for these features, remove the environment variable and any code that passes the secret explicitly. For local development, run vercel env pull . Precomputed codes created without a secret work only in the deployment that created them. Precompute without a secret requires Vercel system environment variables, which are enabled by default. Prebuilt deployments and codes that must work across deployments still need a secret; use FLAGS_PRECOMPUTE_SECRET if only precompute needs one. If you use a build cache, see the precompute documentation for the required configuration. Learn more in the Flags SDK documentation . Read more

title: Agents can now manage AI Gateway through Vercel MCP
description: Your agent can now manage AI Gateway through Vercel MCP . Ask it in plain language to: Manage virtual models : Create reusable model IDs with saved settings, then list, inspect, update, or restore them. Configure routing rules : View, add, and update team-wide rules that redirect requests to another model or block them. Set spending budgets : View and set budgets for your team, projects, and members, and configure defaults. To create a virtual model, for example, ask your agent: Create a virtual model named coding-agent that uses anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 with Zero Data Retention enabled. Your apps and coding agents using AI Gateway can then use vmc/coding-agent as the model ID. You can change its model or settings later without updating those clients or redeploying your app. To get started, connect your agent to Vercel MCP with team-level access and the required AI Gateway permissions. Your Vercel team permissions still apply. Read more
